In this repository, find where "markdown" processing/rendering is defined behind an interface (e.g. an interface/protocol/abstract type for converting markdown to HTML or similar). I need to answer:
1. What is the interface (name, file path)?
2. Which concrete implementation(s) of that interface exist, and are actually constructed/used at runtime (not just tests)?
3. Who constructs/instantiates those implementations (which file/function, e.g. dependency injection wiring, main.go, service constructor)?
4. Which components/structs hold a reference to the interface type (i.e. depend on it)?

Search for terms like "Markdown", "markdown.go", "Renderer", "goldmark", "blackfriday", "MarkdownRenderer" etc. Look at struct field types, interface definitions, and constructor functions (New...). Report concrete file paths and line numbers for: the interface definition, each concrete implementation, the constructor call site(s), and the holder struct(s)/field(s).

Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". 1	package renderer
2	
3	import (
4		"bytes"
5		"fmt"
6		"strings"
7	
8		gast "github.com/yuin/goldmark/ast"
9		east "github.com/yuin/goldmark/extension/ast"
10	
11		mast "github.com/usememos/memos/internal/markdown/ast"
12	)
13	
14	// MarkdownRenderer renders goldmark AST back to markdown text.
15	type MarkdownRenderer struct {
16		buf *bytes.Buffer
17	}
18	
19	// NewMarkdownRenderer creates a new markdown renderer.
20	func NewMarkdownRenderer() *MarkdownRenderer {
21		return &MarkdownRenderer{
22			buf: &bytes.Buffer{},
23		}
24	}
25	
26	// Render renders the AST node to markdown and returns the result.
27	func (r *MarkdownRenderer) Render(node gast.Node, source []byte) string {
28		r.buf.Reset()
29		r.renderNode(node, source, 0)
30		return r.buf.String()
31	}
32	
33	// renderNode renders a single node and its children.
34	func (r *MarkdownRenderer) renderNode(node gast.Node, source []byte, depth int) {
35		switch n := node.(type) {
36		case *gast.Document:
37			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
38	
39		case *gast.Paragraph:
40			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
41			if node.NextSibling() != nil {
42				r.buf.WriteString("\n\n")
43			}
44	
45		case *gast.Text:
46			// Text nodes store their content as segments in the source
47			segment := n.Segment
48			r.buf.Write(segment.Value(source))
49			if n.SoftLineBreak() {
50				r.buf.WriteByte('\n')
51			} else if n.HardLineBreak() {
52				r.buf.WriteString("  \n")
53			}
54	
55		case *gast.CodeSpan:
56			r.buf.WriteByte('`')
57			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
58			r.buf.WriteByte('`')
59	
60		case *gast.Emphasis:
61			symbol := "*"
62			if n.Level == 2 {
63				symbol = "**"
64			}
65			r.buf.WriteString(symbol)
66			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
67			r.buf.WriteString(symbol)
68	
69		case *gast.Link:
70			r.buf.WriteString("[")
71			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
72			r.buf.WriteString("](")
73			r.buf.Write(n.Destination)
74			if len(n.Title) > 0 {
75				r.buf.WriteString(` "`)
76				r.buf.Write(n.Title)
77				r.buf.WriteString(`"`)
78			}
79			r.buf.WriteString(")")
80	
81		case *gast.AutoLink:
82			url := n.URL(source)
83			if n.AutoLinkType == gast.AutoLinkEmail {
84				r.buf.WriteString("<")
85				r.buf.Write(url)
86				r.buf.WriteString(">")
87			} else {
88				r.buf.Write(url)
89			}
90	
91		case *gast.Image:
92			r.buf.WriteString("![")
93			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
94			r.buf.WriteString("](")
95			r.buf.Write(n.Destination)
96			if len(n.Title) > 0 {
97				r.buf.WriteString(` "`)
98				r.buf.Write(n.Title)
99				r.buf.WriteString(`"`)
100			}
101			r.buf.WriteString(")")
102	
103		case *gast.Heading:
104			r.buf.WriteString(strings.Repeat("#", n.Level))
105			r.buf.WriteByte(' ')
106			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
107			if node.NextSibling() != nil {
108				r.buf.WriteString("\n\n")
109			}
110	
111		case *gast.CodeBlock, *gast.FencedCodeBlock:
112			r.renderCodeBlock(n, source)
113	
114		case *gast.Blockquote:
115			// Render each child line with "> " prefix
116			r.renderBlockquote(n, source, depth)
117			if node.NextSibling() != nil {
118				r.buf.WriteString("\n\n")
119			}
120	
121		case *gast.List:
122			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
123			if node.NextSibling() != nil {
124				r.buf.WriteString("\n\n")
125			}
126	
127		case *gast.ListItem:
128			r.renderListItem(n, source, depth)
129	
130		case *gast.ThematicBreak:
131			r.buf.WriteString("---")
132			if node.NextSibling() != nil {
133				r.buf.WriteString("\n\n")
134			}
135	
136		case *east.Strikethrough:
137			r.buf.WriteString("~~")
138			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
139			r.buf.WriteString("~~")
140	
141		case *east.TaskCheckBox:
142			if n.IsChecked {
143				r.buf.WriteString("[x] ")
144			} else {
145				r.buf.WriteString("[ ] ")
146			}
147	
148		case *east.Table:
149			r.renderTable(n, source)
150			if node.NextSibling() != nil {
151				r.buf.WriteString("\n\n")
152			}
153	
154		// Custom Memos nodes
155		case *mast.TagNode:
156			r.buf.WriteByte('#')
157			r.buf.Write(n.Tag)
158	
159		case *mast.MentionNode:
160			r.buf.WriteByte('@')
161			r.buf.Write(n.Username)
162	
163		default:
164			// For unknown nodes, try to render children
165			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
166		}
167	}
168	
169	// renderChildren renders all children of a node.
170	func (r *MarkdownRenderer) renderChildren(node gast.Node, source []byte, depth int) {
171		child := node.FirstChild()
172		for child != nil {
173			r.renderNode(child, source, depth+1)
174			child = child.NextSibling()
175		}
176	}
177	
178	// renderCodeBlock renders a code block.
179	func (r *MarkdownRenderer) renderCodeBlock(node gast.Node, source []byte) {
180		if fenced, ok := node.(*gast.FencedCodeBlock); ok {
181			// Fenced code block with language
182			r.buf.WriteString("```")
183			if lang := fenced.Language(source); len(lang) > 0 {
184				r.buf.Write(lang)
185			}
186			r.buf.WriteByte('\n')
187	
188			// Write all lines
189			lines := fenced.Lines()
190			for i := 0; i < lines.Len(); i++ {
191				line := lines.At(i)
192				r.buf.Write(line.Value(source))
193			}
194	
195			r.buf.WriteString("```")
196			if node.NextSibling() != nil {
197				r.buf.WriteString("\n\n")
198			}
199		} else if codeBlock, ok := node.(*gast.CodeBlock); ok {
200			// Indented code block
201			lines := codeBlock.Lines()
202			for i := 0; i < lines.Len(); i++ {
203				line := lines.At(i)
204				r.buf.WriteString("    ")
205				r.buf.Write(line.Value(source))
206			}
207			if node.NextSibling() != nil {
208				r.buf.WriteString("\n\n")
209			}
210		}
211	}
212	
213	// renderBlockquote renders a blockquote with "> " prefix.
214	func (r *MarkdownRenderer) renderBlockquote(node *gast.Blockquote, source []byte, depth int) {
215		// Create a temporary buffer for the blockquote content
216		tempBuf := &bytes.Buffer{}
217		tempRenderer := &MarkdownRenderer{buf: tempBuf}
218		tempRenderer.renderChildren(node, source, depth)
219	
220		// Add "> " prefix to each line
221		content := tempBuf.String()
222		lines := strings.Split(strings.TrimRight(content, "\n"), "\n")
223		for i, line := range lines {
224			r.buf.WriteString("> ")
225			r.buf.WriteString(line)
226			if i < len(lines)-1 {
227				r.buf.WriteByte('\n')
228			}
229		}
230	}
231	
232	// renderListItem renders a list item with proper indentation and markers.
233	func (r *MarkdownRenderer) renderListItem(node *gast.ListItem, source []byte, depth int) {
234		parent := node.Parent()
235		list, ok := parent.(*gast.List)
236		if !ok {
237			r.renderChildren(node, source, depth)
238			return
239		}
240	
241		// Add indentation only for nested lists
242		// Document=0, List=1, ListItem=2 (no indent), nested ListItem=3+ (indent)
243		if depth > 2 {
244			indent := strings.Repeat("  ", depth-2)
245			r.buf.WriteString(indent)
246		}
247	
248		// Add list marker
249		if list.IsOrdered() {
250			fmt.Fprintf(r.buf, "%d. ", list.Start)
251			list.Start++ // Increment for next item
252		} else {
253			r.buf.WriteString("- ")
254		}
255	
256		// Render content
257		r.renderChildren(node, source, depth)
258	
259		// Add newline if there's a next sibling
260		if node.NextSibling() != nil {
261			r.buf.WriteByte('\n')
262		}
263	}
264	
265	// renderTable renders a table in markdown format.
266	func (r *MarkdownRenderer) renderTable(table *east.Table, source []byte) {
267		// This is a simplified table renderer
268		// A full implementation would need to handle alignment, etc.
269		r.renderChildren(table, source, 0)
270	}

Confirmed: only one concrete implementation, `*service` in `markdown.go` itself, no mocks or alternate implementations elsewhere.

## Findings

### 1. The interface

**`markdown.Service`** — `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go:31-55`

```go
type Service interface {
    ExtractAll(content []byte) (*ExtractedData, error)
    ExtractTags(content []byte) ([]string, error)
    ExtractProperties(content []byte) (*storepb.MemoPayload_Property, error)
    RenderMarkdown(content []byte) (string, error)   // AST -> markdown text
    RenderHTML(content []byte) (string, error)        // markdown -> HTML (goldmark)
    GenerateSnippet(content []byte, maxLength int) (string, error)
    ValidateContent(content []byte) error
    RenameTag(content []byte, oldTag, newTag string) (string, error)
}
```

Package doc comment (lines 27-30) explains: goldmark is used for parsing/metadata extraction; HTML rendering is primarily done client-side via markdown-it, but `RenderHTML` exists server-side for RSS feeds and other server-side rendering needs.

### 2. Concrete implementation(s)

Only one implementation exists, and it's what's constructed at runtime:

- **`*service`** (unexported struct) — `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go:58-60`, wraps `goldmark.Markdown` (field `md`). Methods implementing the interface span lines 116-453 of the same file.
  - Internally it delegates markdown-AST-to-text rendering to a helper type `renderer.MarkdownRenderer` (`/bench/repo/internal/markdown/renderer/markdown_renderer.go:15-24`, constructed via `renderer.NewMarkdownRenderer()`), used inside `service.RenderMarkdown` (markdown.go:250) and `service.RenameTag` (markdown.go:451). Note this `MarkdownRenderer` is not itself the interface implementation — it's a helper used by `*service`, not a `markdown.Service`.
  - HTML conversion (`RenderHTML`, markdown.go:255-261) uses goldmark's own built-in HTML renderer directly (`s.md.Convert`), not a custom renderer type.

No mocks/alternate implementations of `markdown.Service` exist anywhere in the codebase (verified via grep for other `func (s *X)` sets matching the interface signature).

### 3. Constructor / wiring

- **`markdown.NewService(opts ...Option) Service`** — `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go:85-113`. Functional-options constructor (`WithTagExtension`, `WithMentionExtension`) that builds the goldmark instance with GFM + custom tag/mention extensions.
- **Runtime call site**: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:47-62`, inside `NewAPIV1Service(secret, profile, store)`:
  ```go
  markdownService := markdown.NewService(
      markdown.WithTagExtension(),
      markdown.WithMentionExtension(),
  )
  ```
  assigned to `APIV1Service.MarkdownService` (line 56).
- `NewAPIV1Service` itself is invoked from **`/bench/repo/server/server.go:76`**: `apiV1Service := apiv1.NewAPIV1Service(s.Secret, profile, store)` — this is the actual production wiring root (called from the server's `Register`/startup flow).
- The single `markdownService` instance is then passed onward from `apiV1Service.MarkdownService` into `rss.NewRSSService(...)` at **`/bench/repo/server/server.go:85`**, so the whole app shares one `markdown.Service` instance.
- Other `markdown.NewService(...)` call sites are test-only: `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss_test.go:54`, `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver_test.go:427`, `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/test/test_helper.go:44`.

### 4. Holders of the interface (dependents)

- **`APIV1Service`** — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:22-45`, field `MarkdownService markdown.Service` (line 35). Used in:
  - `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108,447` — calls `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload(ctx, ..., s.MarkdownService)`
  - `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go:32` — `s.MarkdownService.ExtractAll(...)` for mention resolution
  - `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:85` — `s.MarkdownService.GenerateSnippet(...)`
- **`RSSService`** — `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go:42-50`, field `MarkdownService markdown.Service` (line 45); constructor `NewRSSService` at line 58; used at line 339 (`s.MarkdownService.RenderHTML(...)`) to render memo content to HTML for RSS feed items.
- **`memopayload.Runner`** — `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:14-17`, field `MarkdownService markdown.Service`; constructor `NewRunner` at line 19. **This holder is effectively dead/unused code** — `NewRunner`/`Runner.RunOnce` are never called anywhere in the codebase outside their own file (unlike the sibling `s3presign.NewRunner(s.Store)`, which is wired into `server/server.go:162`). Only the free function `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload(ctx, memo, markdownService)` (line 74, also in this file) is actually used, called directly from `memo_service.go` with `s.MarkdownService` — it doesn't require the `Runner` struct at all.
